references.text: Moses is commanded to stretch out his hand, a similar command as here where he must stretch out his hand toward the sky to bring hail.
Moses stretches out his hand over Egypt's waters to bring frogs, following the same pattern of stretching out his hand to trigger a plague.
The execution of the command given in verse 22, where Moses stretches out his staff toward the sky and the Lord sends thunder and hail.
A similar command where Moses is to stretch out his hand over Egypt to bring locusts.
Moses is commanded to stretch out his hand toward the sky to bring darkness over Egypt.
The Lord uses hail as an instrument of judgment, similar to its use as a plague over Egypt.
Hail and fire are cast upon the earth, an eschatological parallel to the plague of hail in Egypt.
Great hail falls from heaven upon people, alluding to the Egyptian plague of hail.
Both verses in chapter 9 describe actions directed toward the sky to trigger a plague, showing variation in how God's judgment is manifested.
Verse 10:22 shows the actual execution of the prophetic action (hand toward the sky) commanded in 9:22, even though the plagues are different.
